title: docker push
definition: The CLI command used to upload a locally built Docker image to a remote Docker registry (like Docker Hub or AWS ECR).
simpleExplanation: Uploading your finished blueprint to the cloud so other computers can download it.
realWorldExample: You finish writing code on your laptop. You build the image. You type `docker push myusername/my-app:v2`. Docker uploads the layers to the internet. Now your boss can pull the image and test it.

basic: What happens if you run `docker push` before running `docker login`?
intermediate: If an image has 10 layers, and you only changed 1 line of code, does `docker push` upload all 10 layers again?

answers.question: Push without login?
answers.answer: Docker will throw an 'Access Denied / Unauthorized' error because it doesn't know who you are.

answers.question: Upload all layers?
answers.answer: No! Docker is smart. It checks the Registry, sees that the first 9 layers are already uploaded, and only uploads the tiny 1 new layer. This makes pushing updates incredibly fast.
